method: Read actual public browser exports; normal E.importSave validates source/prepared-raw-final/actual/policy-adopted-expected saves by authoritative create-and-command replay. Replay each actual UI command suffix from the unchanged checkpoint. Separately construct the current public import workflow with explicit engine applyChapelRuling/applyCombatReactionRuling/applyTileSpeedRuling commands, then replay the planned UI actions. Compare entire policy-adopted state after only empty optional ATTACK/COUNTER command-record arrays normalization, plus full gameplay facts and public DOM routing.
normalizationBoundary: Only remove empty itemIds/pullIds/rewardIds arrays on recorded ATTACK or COUNTER commands. No authoritative rule-state field, mission, event, RNG, deck, combat or pending followup is normalized, ignored or edited. Import policy is applied as an accepted recorded engine command, not ignored or hidden.
preparationCorrection: Original checkpoint expectation helper used raw E.importSave and omitted hunt-app applyLoadedRuling. All nine actual public imports added APPLY_TILE_SPEED_RULING; this legitimately adds one revision and tileSpeedRuling=all-attacks. Original expected files were retained. A separate policy-adopted expected file is replayed and validated for each scenario. This is an expectation-preparation difference, not a demonstrated game defect.
presentationCounterInterpretation: Public DOM host presentationAttacks/presentationMoves are cumulative adapter counters across imports; they were not treated as per-scenario motion totals. Routing validation uses exact actor IDs, skin IDs and logical nodes. Root owns visual frame inspection.

finalScaleFollowup.method: Normal E.importSave validates source, original actual export, final-size actual export and a normal policy-adopted planned replay export. Replay actual suffix with E.dispatch; compare entire states and preserve original nine-scenario totals.

runtimeMetadata.source: Parent performed final-size browser replay; current atlas/manifest and named-boss renderer contain the display metadata. These fields are presentation metadata, not save-state edits.
